 Proposal for GSoC2013: "rapport" and "pander" packages
    "Gergely Daróczi" <ger...@snowl.net> Mar 21 01:27PM -0700  

    Dear All,
     
    I have just uploaded a proposal about some of our packages at
    http://rwiki.sciviews.org/doku.php?id=developers:projects:gsoc2013:rapport and
    I would be really happy if the R Community would find these packages worth
    to list among this year's proposed projects.
     
    To be honest, I was very busy with reading all the docs about how to apply
    to GSoC individually as an organization when I have found the central GSoC
    hub on the R wiki site, and came to know about this great idea so that R
    related projects could apply for GSoC together.
     
    Please let me know if my proposal would fit the main goals of the
    collective so that I could also update the table at the bottom of the
    http://rwiki.sciviews.org/doku.php?id=developers:projects:gsoc2013 page and
    if there would be anything more I should do now, or if I should rather try
    to apply for GSoC separately.
     
    I already have a proposed student who could help with the listed ideas, but
    of course I would be very happy to see any assistance in the projects.
     
    Best,
    Gergely

     

 Project proposal GSoC13/R: clean-room re-coding of the Akima interpolation algorithm(s)
    Brian Davidson <bkd...@gmail.com> Mar 21 12:52PM -0700  

    I would be interested in taking on this challenge. I am a 2nd degree
    student getting a degree from this program: Oregon State University online
    computer science <http://eecs.oregonstate.edu/novel-online-degree>. My 1st
    degree was in Economics, and have done work in the statistics field. Right
    now I am wrapping up my algorithms course, where I have a very high grade.
    I've programmed in Java, C, bash, sed/awk, and SAS (for work) mostly, but
    also have dabbled in others such as: Scheme, Haskell, Go, and Python. As
    far as R goes, I have done some small statistics based projects using the
    S4 object model (made a number system converter). While Akima's is new to
    me, I am confident that my programming skills are more than sufficient to
    tackle this problem and deliver a sorely needed addition to the R community.
     
    I was wondering if I sounded like the candidate you are looking for. I've
    completed and done well in my programming courses, data structures,
    discrete math, systems architecture, and now Operating Systems and
    Algorithms. I am the kind of person who is given a problem and I don't just
    deliver a solution. I deliver a solution I can justify and fully explain.
